notes:
VW up! family electric cars: e-Up, Citigo-e iV and Mii electric, read over the OBD-II socket's 11-bit CAN at 500 kbit/s with UDS.

The identifier pairs come from two community sources, recorded in docs/vehicles/vag-group.md: the GoingElectric wiki's e-Up OBD2 code list (CC BY-NC-SA, German, 17 units, the primary source) and the Open Vehicle Monitoring System's vweup_obd.h (MIT, 12 units, polled by a module developed against the e-Up). Neither is a Volkswagen document. Each unit's description starts with its VAG logical address, which both sources give for the units they name. Nine units agree between the two sources, five are listed by GoingElectric only and three are in conflict: the brake booster (address 23), the steering assist (44) and the brake sensors (AD) share a request identifier but differ in the response identifier. GoingElectric's response is the request plus 0x6A, which is the offset every pair outside the 0x7E0 to 0x7E7 request block uses in both sources and in the MQB table (inside that block it is plus 0x08); OVMS's is the request plus 0x08 for these three only. That pattern favours GoingElectric but proves neither, so the GoingElectric value is shipped and the OVMS value is in the unit's description.

The petrol up!, Mii and Citigo have no source of their own and are not covered. Units without a CAN pair in either source (04, 08, 09, 19, 56, 61) are left out. The default session, which every UDS unit must accept, is the one opened. Treat every row as unconfirmed until `obd-read probe` shows the unit answering.
name: vw-up
description: Volkswagen up! electric family (e-Up, Citigo-e iV, Mii electric), UDS over CAN

vin.source: The WMIs are the makers' car and SUV identifiers in the world manufacturer identifier table of the Wikipedia article Vehicle identification number, which cites the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt manufacturer list SV 3.2 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number, archived https://web.archive.org/web/20261102120229/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number). A WMI names the maker and plant, not the model, so a match only says the car is of a make this profile covers.

motor-electronics.description: VAG address 01: Motor electronics (Motorelektronik); the OVMS file calls it the motor electronics and reads the drive state, speed, state of charge and temperatures
